name: Plague of Justinian
summary: The first pandemic of bubonic plague strikes the Byzantine Empire beginning in Egypt (541), spreading through the Mediterranean world in waves over 200 years. At its height in Constantinople (542), contemporary sources describe 5,000–10,000 deaths per day; the population of the Eastern Empire may have fallen by 25–50%. The plague repeatedly disrupts Justinian's reconquests by eliminating troops and tax base. The pandemics continue until 750, contributing to the weakening of the Byzantine and Sasanian Empires that allows the Arab conquests to succeed.

_quarry.structural_significance: First global pandemic of bubonic plague; kills perhaps a third of the Byzantine Empire's population; disrupts Justinian's reconquests; weakens both Byzantine and Sasanian Empires, contributing to the success of the Arab conquests
